messages:
Maria G: FYI - customer on enterprise tier reports that after today's rollout their assistant is dropping earlier instructions in long chats. They say it used to follow system instructions across ~6k tokens, now it forgets after ~2k and starts hallucinating. Example and repro below.

Aj Patel: Can you paste the original prompt + model name + request_id? also any customer logs?

Maria G: Customer provided this minimal repro (redacted user text):

```
system: You are a helpful assistant. Always respond in bullet points and never mention policy.
user: Here's a long doc (pasted, ~5.6k tokens). Then a short followup: "Summarize the key action items."
```

Model used: rwd-13b-v2 (we rolled rwd-13b-v2 optimized at 07:15 UTC today)
Customer request_id: req_01F8a2X9Z
Response they got (truncated): "... summary: 1) do X 2) do Y" then it starts making up an unrelated new requirement and ignores the instruction style.

Aj Patel: Got it. I'm pulling logs for req_01F8a2X9Z. Can you confirm whether they set `max_tokens` or `max_output_tokens`? And did they use streaming?

Maria G: They set `max_output_tokens: 1024`, streaming: false. No special routing.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: canary rollout rwd-13b-v2-optimized -> 30% @ 07:15 UTC.

Aj Patel: Checked logs for req_01F8a2X9Z. Relevant excerpts: 

```
[2026-02-24T07:22:10Z] req_01F8a2X9Z init model=rwd-13b-v2-optimized seq_total=5620 client=acct_4B
[2026-02-24T07:22:11Z] kv_cache_alloc size=2048KB per_shard=256KB
[2026-02-24T07:22:13Z] generation start len(prompt)=5600 target=1024
[2026-02-24T07:22:18Z] warning: attention_cache_trim activated at token_idx=2048
[2026-02-24T07:22:19Z] generation truncated prefix_tokens=2048 -> effective_prompt_len=2048
[2026-02-24T07:22:19Z] gen finished reason=length tokens_generated=512
```

Aj Patel: Looks like the runtime trimmed the prefix at 2048 tokens (attention cache trimming). That explains lost instructions. Need to know why trimming threshold changed. Before rollout threshold was 8192 in our perf profile.

Olivia H: I saw the canary update earlier. We shipped a new kernel selection path that adjusts KV shard sizes dynamically to reduce memory for fp16 quantized runs. Possible bug: the allocator misreports available memory for multi-shard configs which forces aggressive trimming.

Kevin L: Quick Q for support: is the customer on Dedicated or Hosted? If Dedicated we might have different memory config per pool.

Maria G: Hosted (regular enterprise account). Customer says no other errors, but increased response time by ~100ms for these requests after rollout. No billing spikes.

Olivia H: Repro locally with canary configuration? I need a minimized curl from them. Maria can you ask for a reproducible request (with sanitized content) and the exact headers?

Maria G: Sent them a repro template. Customer returned this curl (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "rwd-13b-v2-optimized",
    "input": "<LONG_DOCUMENT_PLACEHOLDER>",
    "max_output_tokens": 1024,
    "temperature": 0.0
  }'
```

Aj Patel: Tried repro on staging with canary flag enabled. Observed same behavior: attention_cache_trim at ~2048 tokens. I also see a config diff in the rollout: default `kv_cache_limit_mb` went from 16384 -> 2048 in the canary profile by mistake (unit mismatch). That would explain the aggressive trim.

Olivia H: Ugh that looks like a release config bug. The new optimizer was supposed to use 16GB but config read it as 2GB. Root cause: config parser interprets shorthand values differently when `memory_profile: auto` flag is set. Fix incoming.

Kevin L: Mitigation for affected customers: revert routing back to previous model variant (rwd-13b-v2-stable) OR pin them to a dedicated pool that still has the old profile.

Aj Patel: I'll apply a temporary routing override for acct_4B to force stable variant and notify customer. Also adding a transparent note in the response: "We're reverting a recent optimization that affected long-context behavior." Drafting message now.

sre-oncall: Please also check autoscaler/burst capacity - if we revert routes to stable it might increase memory demand. Monitor pod mem by pool.

support-bot: Escalation ticket created: INC-2026-4921. Priority: P1. Assigned: eng-runtime, infra, support.

Maria G: Customer update sent: asked them to repro after ~10min and confirm. They answered: immediate improvement after routing override, earlier instructions preserved in the same long chat. They're happy for now but want postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

Olivia H: I'll open a patch to the config parser and test with long-context suites (3k-10k tokens). Will also add a guard to prevent memory values below expected thresholds for known long-context models.

Kevin L: Can someone drop the exact commit and canary id so ops can roll it back if needed?

Olivia H: Patch PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4981. Canary id: canary-2026-02-24-0715. Revert plan ready.

Aj Patel: Closing loop: customer notified, routing override applied, mitigated. Next steps: eng-runtime to patch + rollout, QA to run long-context regression suite, support to update customer when patch is live.

Maria G: adding customer asks: written assurance + brief explanation of root cause and steps to prevent recurrence. I'll follow up and attach postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:
